AnalyticsCountView.description:
One grouping key and how many events fell under it. ``key`` names
whichever dimension this response is grouped by — a file path, a skill name, an
agent type, or a node id. ``graph_name`` and ``node_name`` name what a node-keyed row
counts: null on the files, skills, and agent-types dimensions, which have no graph or
node, and null where the node id no longer resolves. Under ``by_name`` the row is the
roll-up of every minted id sharing the name pair, and ``key`` is ``<graph_name>/<node_name>``.
AnalyticsCountView.title: AnalyticsCountView

AnalyticsCountsResponse.description:
Every grouping key matching the filters, most-frequent first with the key
ascending as the tiebreak — a total order two identical calls agree on.
AnalyticsCountsResponse.title: AnalyticsCountsResponse

AnalyticsSpendResponse.description:
Every grouping key matching the filters, key ascending — a total order two
identical calls agree on, the same convention the durations/counts responses use.
AnalyticsSpendResponse.title: AnalyticsSpendResponse

AnalyticsSpendView.description:
One grouping key's usage/cost rollup — ``key`` is a node id or a graph id, whichever dataset
served it. The same contract ``GET /api/spend`` publishes: ``cost_partial`` is ``True`` iff some summed
row carried neither a billed nor an estimated amount, and ``estimated_cost_usd`` is ``None`` unless some
summed row carried one. ``graph_name`` and ``node_name`` name what the row sums, null where an
id no longer resolves and ``node_name`` always null on a graph row: a node row names the node's
own graph, a graph row names the chunk's *current* pin, so a migrated chunk's two rows can
disagree. Under ``by_name`` the row rolls up every minted id sharing the name, and ``key`` is
``<graph_name>/<node_name>`` for a node and ``graph_name`` for a graph.
AnalyticsSpendView.title: AnalyticsSpendView

ArtifactScope.description:
Where an artifact is pinned — a chunk's node-step, the graph mint that baked it into
the graph itself (``artifacts:``), or blizzard's own published, global-namespace
documents, resolved at call time (``system``).
ArtifactScope.title: ArtifactScope

ArtifactView.description:
One entry of a chunk's inline artifact store. ``key`` is ``{node}.{artifact-name}.{epoch}`` —
append-only, so latest-by-epoch resolution is the reader's. ``content`` carries an **asset**'s text
verbatim; ``repo``/``branch_name``/``commit_hash`` carry a ``git_commit``'s pinned reference, never
the code. ``branch_url`` is the branch's forge URL. ``recorded_at`` decodes the id's ULID stamp.
ArtifactView.title: ArtifactView

AskListResponse.description: Every ask still awaiting an answer.
AskListResponse.title: AskListResponse

AskRequest.description: A worker's ask: the question and its optional pipe-separated choices.
AskRequest.title: AskRequest

AskResponse.description: The recorded ask — its minted question id.
AskResponse.title: AskResponse

AttachmentRequest.description: A worker's explicit artifact submission for one ``produces:`` name.
AttachmentRequest.title: AttachmentRequest

BlockedView.description:
A chunk's blocked marking — present iff a pre-claim dependent (``not_ready`` or
``ready``) has a standing dependency edge naming a prerequisite that has not reached ``done``.
Carried beside ``status``, never a status of its own; names the immediate prerequisite only, with
no transitive walk to whatever it may itself wait on. Where several prerequisites are unmet at
once, ``prerequisite_chunk_id`` names the earliest-declared one. The marking is absent when
nothing is unmet.

unmet_count.description: The count of unmet prerequisites, never below 1.
unmet_count.title: Unmet Count

BlockedView.title: BlockedView

BounceView.description:
One recorded delivery kick-back (#64) — contention, not failure, and never itself a status.
``envelope`` is the raw JSON kick-back payload verbatim.
BounceView.title: BounceView

ChunkAskView.description:
One question asked on a chunk, open or answered. ``node`` is the asking node's name,
falling back to its raw id when the payload names no node by that id.
ChunkAskView.title: ChunkAskView

ChunkDetail.description:
The whole chunk aggregate: transition history, inline artifact
store, and the open escalation.
ChunkDetail.title: ChunkDetail

ChunkEscalationView.description:
An open escalation on a ``needs_human`` chunk — the takeover command(s) for the parked session,
present only while the escalation is open — a later lease mint, requeue, or completion supersedes it.
``wrapped_takeover_command`` is optional, empty when none was composed.
ChunkEscalationView.title: ChunkEscalationView

ChunkNeighborView.description:
One standing-edge neighbor, one hop away. ``status`` is null only for
the residual race a neighbor's facts fail to resolve — the edge is still drawn,
unsatisfied, rather than dropped. See BlockedView for the immediate-only, no-transitive
scope this shares.
ChunkNeighborView.title: ChunkNeighborView

ChunkNeighborhoodView.description:
A chunk's standing dependency edges one hop each way — both
``prerequisites`` and ``dependents`` are always present as lists, empty rather than
null.
ChunkNeighborhoodView.title: ChunkNeighborhoodView

ChunkStatus.description: The derived chunk statuses. Never stored — always a query result.
ChunkStatus.title: ChunkStatus

ChunkSummary.description:
One row of the fleet chunk list — the derived status and current node. ``current_node_name`` is
the node's human graph name beside the raw ``nd_`` ULID, null when unresolvable.
``runner_id``/``environment_count`` are **in-progress-only**: a terminal chunk reads
unrouted even while its route facts stand. ``completed_at`` is the terminal instant, else null.
ChunkSummary.title: ChunkSummary

ChunkUsageTotalView.description:
A chunk's derived usage/cost total, summed over every recorded invocation — never a stored column.
``cost_partial`` is ``True`` iff some summed row carries neither a billed nor an estimated amount;
``billed_partial`` iff some carries no billed amount, so ``cost_usd`` is then a lower bound of billed
spend. ``estimated_cost_usd`` is ``None`` iff no row carried one, and never enters ``cost_usd``.
ChunkUsageTotalView.title: ChunkUsageTotalView

ChunkUsageView.description:
One node-step's usage/cost telemetry — one harness invocation's tokens-by-class and
cost. ``cost_usd`` is ``None`` exactly when no billed figure was
recorded for this invocation — never fabricated. ``estimated_cost_usd`` is the runner's own reported
estimate for a subscription invocation, kept apart from ``cost_usd``, ``None`` when none was reported.
ChunkUsageView.title: ChunkUsageView

DashboardView.description:
``GET /api/dashboard`` — nine status reads composed into one response.
``fleet_summary`` alone is a hub pass-through and the only nullable section —
``None`` on a hub failure or an unwired runner, while the eight local sections
still populate.
DashboardView.title: DashboardView

DecisionView.description:
A gate decision in full.

``resolved_choice`` is set once a person has decided; ``transitioned`` is true once the
resolving transition has been recorded.
DecisionView.title: DecisionView

EnvironmentListResponse.description: Every environment in the runner's configured pool, held or free.
EnvironmentListResponse.title: EnvironmentListResponse

EnvironmentView.description:
One environment in the runner's configured pool — ``GET /api/environments``.
``chunk_id``/``held_since`` are present only while the environment
is currently bound; an unused pool environment carries both as ``None``. ``held`` is the
runner's own reading of whether a chunk holds it, so no client re-derives it.
EnvironmentView.title: EnvironmentView

EscalationListResponse.description: Every escalation still open — no later lease mint, and the hub has not ended the chunk.
EscalationListResponse.title: EscalationListResponse

EscalationView.description: One parked escalation, carrying its literal takeover command — ``GET /api/escalations``.
EscalationView.title: EscalationView

FactChangedPayload.description:
A hub-bound fact was enqueued or acked — mirrors the hub's own ``event-logged``
shape: ``chunk_id``/``lease_id`` ride as a present ``null`` rather than omitted,
since a runner-wide fact (e.g. a chunk-less ``event.recorded``) legitimately carries
neither. Never a heartbeat — those ride elsewhere, elapsed-time-derived.
FactChangedPayload.title: FactChangedPayload

FactListResponse.description: The most recent hub-bound facts, newest first.
FactListResponse.title: FactListResponse

FactView.description:
One hub-bound fact off the runner store's outbound buffer — ``GET /api/facts``.

The local fact log: the record itself minus its JSON ``payload``. ``acked_at``
null means still buffered.
FactView.title: FactView

FindingExit.description:
How an exited finding left: ``outflow`` when the ground itself changed, ``withdrawn``
when a person judged the finding rather than the code.
FindingExit.title: FindingExit

FindingSource.description: A finding's home — the routine run or the chunk review that raised it.
FindingSource.title: FindingSource

FindingState.description:
A finding's derived liveness — ``live`` for a live-making newest fact, else the newest
fact's own kind.
FindingState.title: FindingState

FindingView.description:
A finding. `state` folds the newest fact's kind to `"live"` for
`add`/`observed`/`reopened`; `note` is that fact's own note. `source`
is `"routine"` or `"review"`: a review-sourced finding carries no
`routine_name`, its own `severity`, and the `raised_by_chunk_id` that raised it.
FindingView.title: FindingView

FleetSummaryView.title: FleetSummaryView

GardenProposalClosureKind.description:
How a garden proposal closed — recorded on the row itself when it closes, never
derived from anything else.
GardenProposalClosureKind.title: GardenProposalClosureKind

GardenProposalClosureView.description:
How a garden proposal closed — a pass or an accept, either way
terminal.
GardenProposalClosureView.title: GardenProposalClosureView

GardenProposalItemOutcome.description:
Whether an accepted proposal minted a work item — recorded positively rather than
inferred from an absent link, so a declined mint reads as a decision, not a gap.
GardenProposalItemOutcome.title: GardenProposalItemOutcome

GardenProposalOrigin.description:
Who authored a garden proposal — a mint-time fact, stored on
the row itself and never inferred from a null `routine_name`.
GardenProposalOrigin.title: GardenProposalOrigin

GardenProposalView.description:
A garden proposal, its closure carried alongside it once one exists.
`routine_name` is nullable — an operator-authored proposal may name
no routine; `created_by` is set only for one.
GardenProposalView.title: GardenProposalView

GitCommitDeclarationRequest.description:
A worker's explicit git-commit declaration for one repo it touched.

Carries no forge: the origin verified against is read from the environment's
repo manifest. ``environment_id`` is required once a chunk holds several.
GitCommitDeclarationRequest.title: GitCommitDeclarationRequest

GitCommitDeclarationResponse.description:
``POST /api/leases/{lease_id}/git-commits`` — the declaration landed durably.
``note`` is set when it lands but rides no completion — declared against the closed
reference lease an open takeover names.
GitCommitDeclarationResponse.title: GitCommitDeclarationResponse

HarnessHealthListResponse.description: Every configured harness binding's own computed health.
HarnessHealthListResponse.title: HarnessHealthListResponse

HarnessHealthView.description:
One configured harness binding's own computed health —
``GET /api/harness-health``, runner-local diagnostics only. ``cause`` is one of
``missing_binary``, ``incompatible_version``, ``unknown_version``, ``authentication_failure``,
``config_conflict``, ``unmapped_tier``, or ``selftest_failure`` when unavailable; ``declared_degradation`` when
available but degraded; ``None`` only when available with no declared degradation either.
HarnessHealthView.title: HarnessHealthView

HarnessSignalStatus.description:
One signal of the harness bindings' telemetry: what the enabled bindings together do with its exporter, and
what the runner's receiver for it has accepted and dropped since start, in that signal's own unit.
HarnessSignalStatus.title: HarnessSignalStatus

HarnessTelemetryOutcome.description: What the runner does with one of a harness binding's telemetry signals.
HarnessTelemetryOutcome.title: HarnessTelemetryOutcome

HeartbeatRequest.description: A worker's heartbeat: the lease it inherited at spawn (``BLIZZARD_LEASE_ID``).
HeartbeatRequest.title: HeartbeatRequest

HistoryRowView.description:
One row of a chunk's own timeline — a transition, a cross-graph migration, or a
delivery bounce, merged oldest-first by ``recorded_at``. ``from_node``/``to_node`` are
node labels (a migration's is a ``graph/node`` hop), both null for a bounce; ``epoch``
is transition-only; ``cause``/``detail`` carry a bounce's kick-back or a migration source.
HistoryRowView.title: HistoryRowView

HubConnectivityView.description:
Hub reachability (derived, not probed) plus the outbound backlog depth.

``endpoint`` is the configured hub base URL — connectivity facts, not a probe.
HubConnectivityView.title: HubConnectivityView

IntendedMigrationView.description:
A chunk's standing migration intent — editable at any non-terminal status and
consulted, never applied eagerly, at the chunk's next transition. ``graph_name`` is resolved
server-side from the stored ``graph_id``, null when unresolvable. ``node_name`` is the ``forced``
mode's landing target, null for ``auto``, whose landing is derived at consult time.
IntendedMigrationView.title: IntendedMigrationView

LandedRepoView.description: One repo's actual merged revision; URL absent without a known PR forge.
LandedRepoView.title: LandedRepoView

LeaseClosureReason.description: The published ``lease_closures.reason`` values; the store-only mint reasons are not among them.
LeaseClosureReason.title: LeaseClosureReason

LeaseView.description:
One lease — active or recently-closed — with its joined binding facts and
derived state.
LeaseView.title: LeaseView

MigrationMode.description:
How a chunk's intended migration fires at its next transition.

``AUTO`` fires only when the transition's own destination node name also exists on
the target graph; ``FORCED`` fires unconditionally onto the intent's ``node_name``.
MigrationMode.title: MigrationMode

MigrationSource.description:
What moved a chunk onto another graph — a migration's attribution.

Four paths write one, and without a discriminator their facts are byte-identical
in history.
MigrationSource.title: MigrationSource

MigrationView.description:
One cross-graph migration step: the chunk was re-pinned from ``from_graph`` onto
``landed_node`` in ``to_graph`` — its own step, never a transition. A transition-borne source ends
the attempt and re-queues; ``restart`` preempts it and keeps the route. ``model`` is the
re-pinned model, null when the chunk kept its own. ``source`` attributes it, and ``epoch``
records the submitting step's epoch for an authored-edge migration.
MigrationView.title: MigrationView

OpenTakeoverListResponse.description: Every takeover still open across this runner's held chunks.
OpenTakeoverListResponse.title: OpenTakeoverListResponse

OpenTakeoverView.description:
One open operator takeover — ``GET /api/takeovers``, the stranded-takeover
recovery surface: the chunk it holds, the ``takeover_id`` an
interrupted terminal never PATCHed closed, and how long it has been held.
OpenTakeoverView.title: OpenTakeoverView

PauseStateView.description:
The pause brake's two independent surfaces, plus their effective OR.

``local_reason`` is the local brake's own reason — a usage limit, the spend ceiling, or
``None`` on a plain operator pause.
PauseStateView.title: PauseStateView

PauseView.description:
An open pause on a chunk — who set it and when, present only while ``paused=True``
is the newest pause fact. Carried independently of ``status``: PAUSED sits below the human-gated
statuses in the derivation order, so this is the only carrier of a pause on a gated chunk.
PauseView.title: PauseView

PendingView.description:
A hub node's in-progress poll — whether a chunk parked at a hub node is about to run its
first attempt or is already mid-poll, and when the next is due. Never itself a status.
PendingView.title: PendingView

PrView.description: A repo's PR reference, open or historical according to its containing field.
PrView.title: PrView

QuestionView.title: QuestionView

ReadinessResponse.description: The wire shape of a readiness reading.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ReceiverStatus.description:
The runner's span receiver since it started: worker spans accepted into its export pipeline, and
spans refused — out of step, off allowlist, or over a cap.
ReceiverStatus.title: ReceiverStatus

RenewalFailureReason.description:
The closed set of reasons a due renewal attempt did not succeed: ``renewer_unavailable``,
no renewer could be run; ``timed_out``, the attempt overran its bound; ``vendor_refused``,
the vendor declined to refresh; ``protocol_error``, the vendor's answer was unintelligible.
RenewalFailureReason.title: RenewalFailureReason

RenewalResult.description:
What one renewal attempt is known to have come to. ``RENEWED`` and ``FAILED`` are a
recorded outcome; ``UNRECORDED`` is an attempt with no outcome on record — still in flight,
or its outcome lost to a crash or a failed write.
RenewalResult.title: RenewalResult

RestartView.description:
One operator restart (#370, #371): the chunk was forced from ``from_node`` onto ``to_node`` at
``epoch``, tearing down whatever attempt was running. Its own step, never a transition — nothing
judged it. ``graph_id`` is where it landed, a cross-graph move's target, and ``from_graph`` the graph
it departed, null when it crossed none; ``decision_id`` names the gate decision it closed, or null.
RestartView.title: RestartView

RouteView.description: A chunk's route — where it is being worked.
RouteView.title: RouteView

RunnerAuthSessionView.description:
An own-identity read (``GET /api/auth/session``): whether the human surface is gated
at all, and if so the signed-in hub username. ``auth_enabled`` false is a ``none``-mode hub, whose
surface is authless; ``username`` is ``None`` when gated but no valid session is presented.
RunnerAuthSessionView.title: RunnerAuthSessionView

RunnerControlPatch.description: Declarative controls on the runner singleton — ``paused`` now, routing knobs post-MVP.
RunnerControlPatch.title: RunnerControlPatch

RunnerControlView.description: The runner singleton's derived pause state.
RunnerControlView.title: RunnerControlView

RunnerEventType.description: Every runner SSE frame kind — the ``event:`` name a frame carries.
RunnerEventType.title: RunnerEventType

RunnerStatusView.description: ``GET /api/runner`` — identity, pause states, capacities, hub connectivity, last tick.
RunnerStatusView.title: RunnerStatusView

RunnerTraceReplayFailure.description:
The exporter refused or raised: ``leases``, ``spans`` and ``batches`` count what it accepted before the
replay stopped. ``detail`` is fixed text, never the exporter's own error.
RunnerTraceReplayFailure.title: RunnerTraceReplayFailure

RunnerTraceReplayResponse.description: What a replay told, or with ``dry_run`` would have told.
RunnerTraceReplayResponse.title: RunnerTraceReplayResponse

RunnerTraceStatusResponse.description: The shared status body, plus the runner's harness-telemetry read; ``None`` where the plan is not wired.
RunnerTraceStatusResponse.title: RunnerTraceStatusResponse

SampleMissReason.description:
The closed set of reasons one sampling attempt produced nothing:
``credential_lapsed``, a token past its own expiry or a 401; ``credential_unreadable``, a
missing, malformed, or incomplete credential file; ``endpoint_unreachable``, any other
non-2xx or a request-level failure; ``response_unparseable``, a 2xx body without windows.
SampleMissReason.title: SampleMissReason

ScopeView.description: A scope as served by the create/list/read/lifecycle routes.
ScopeView.title: ScopeView

SelfTestStartRequest.description: Which coding harness to run the canary against.
SelfTestStartRequest.title: SelfTestStartRequest

SelfTestView.description: A selftest run's current state — ``running`` until every check has resolved.
SelfTestView.title: SelfTestView

SidechainSegmentView.description:
A subagent's private conversation, nested under the tool call that spawned it, or
carried on its own ``sidechain`` turn when no spawning call resolved. Recursive: a
sidechain turn may itself carry a tool call whose own sidechain nests further.
SidechainSegmentView.title: SidechainSegmentView

StagedAttachment.description:
One of the lease's currently staged (not-yet-published) submissions —
``GET /api/leases/{lease_id}/attachments``.
StagedAttachment.title: StagedAttachment

SubscriptionListResponse.description: Every declared subscription's own newest sampling attempt.
SubscriptionListResponse.title: SubscriptionListResponse

SubscriptionView.description:
One declared subscription's runner-local diagnostics, served by
``GET /api/subscriptions``. The sampling fields are ``None`` until a first attempt, the
``renewal_*`` fields until a first renewal; each ``*_reason`` is set only on a miss or failure.
SubscriptionView.title: SubscriptionView

TakeoverOpenResponse.description:
``POST /chunks/{id}/takeovers`` — ``command`` is exec'd verbatim in ``workdir``.
``env`` is the bounded takeover env — the lease's ``BLIZZARD_*`` identity
(including the re-minted lease token) plus ``PATH``/``HOME``, never the daemon's full
child env. It rides only this body; the ``command`` string stays printable-safe.
TakeoverOpenResponse.title: TakeoverOpenResponse

TakeoverRequest.description: The takeover request body — ``force`` kills a live worker attempt first.
TakeoverRequest.title: TakeoverRequest

ToolCallSegmentView.description: A tool invocation, structured: what was called, with what input, and what came back.
ToolCallSegmentView.title: ToolCallSegmentView

TraceReplayRequest.description:
The half-open window ``[since, until)`` to tell again — a ``trace-window-skipped`` event's own
``since``/``until`` pastes straight in. ``dry_run`` counts what would be told and exports nothing.
TraceReplayRequest.title: TraceReplayRequest

TranscriptResponse.description:
A lease's parsed transcript — 200 when the lease exists and its recorded harness
owner is known and available; 503 when that owner is unknown or unavailable.
TranscriptResponse.title: TranscriptResponse

TranscriptSegmentContentView.description:
One segment's decompressed turns, concatenated across its stored records in
turn-range order — the lazy per-segment content read.
TranscriptSegmentContentView.title: TranscriptSegmentContentView

TranscriptSegmentIndexEntry.description:
One segment's metadata row — byte counts and completion state, never turn
content. ``truncated`` is true iff any record was cap-rejected OR the runner
itself declared ``record_truncated`` on one, so a consumer can tell an incomplete
segment from a short one without fetching it.
TranscriptSegmentIndexEntry.title: TranscriptSegmentIndexEntry

TranscriptSegmentIndexView.description:
The per-chunk segment discovery read — unreachable content, only what a
caller needs to then ask for one segment's turns.
TranscriptSegmentIndexView.title: TranscriptSegmentIndexView

TransitionView.description:
One accepted transition in a chunk's history: the edge a node-step took — origin node, the
judgement choice that routed it, destination — oldest first on the detail.
``from_node_name``/``to_node_name`` are the nodes' human graph names, null when unresolvable.
``graph_id``/``graph_name`` name the graph this step happened in, both null on old rows.
TransitionView.title: TransitionView

TurnSegmentView.description:
One normalized turn, carried in full. ``index`` is **segment-relative** and producer-minted,
stable across a segment's batches — EXCEPT under ``sidechain.turns``, where it restarts at 0 within
that one sidechain, and on a lease transcript read, where it numbers only the turns that read
returned and slides with the recency window. ``kind`` is closed.
TurnSegmentView.title: TurnSegmentView

WorkItemAuthorView.description:
Who filed a hub-owned work item, legible for display — ``user_id``
and ``login`` set only for ``kind == "user"``; ``runner_id``/``chunk_id``/``node_name``
— the proposing runner, chunk, and node — set only for ``kind == "fleet"``, with
``runner_name`` the proposing runner's latest registered name when the registry holds it.
WorkItemAuthorView.title: WorkItemAuthorView

WorkItemEntry.description:
One pointer's pass-through work item, vendor-native — title, body, comments, and,
only when the source has them to give, ``author``/``stated_priority``.
``label``/``web_url`` are the legible pointer label and browser address, both null when no
configured source names ``source``; a per-pointer failure nulls ``title``/``body`` into ``error``.
WorkItemEntry.title: WorkItemEntry

WorkItemPriority.description: The three stated-priority values a create or edit may set.
WorkItemPriority.title: WorkItemPriority

WorkItemsView.description:
A chunk's pass-through work items — one entry per pointer, order preserved.

Empty when the chunk holds no pointers; a grouped chunk carrying many pointers
yields one entry per pointer, each fetched fresh and never stored.
WorkItemsView.title: WorkItemsView

WorkRefView.title: WorkRefView

WorkerArtifact.description:
One artifact, node- or graph-scoped. A node-scope row is resolved latest-by-epoch
and names its producing node and epoch; a graph-scope row is one of the pinned graph
mint's own baked-in declarations and carries neither, since no node-step produced it.
WorkerArtifact.title: WorkerArtifact

WorkspacePromptReplacement.description: A replacement workspace prompt — applies to subsequent spawns with no restart.
WorkspacePromptReplacement.title: WorkspacePromptReplacement

WorkspacePromptResponse.description: The effective workspace prompt prepended to a worker spawn.
WorkspacePromptResponse.title: WorkspacePromptResponse

get.description:
Every ask still awaiting an answer — ``GET /api/asks?open=true``.

The one **human-web-lane** route on this otherwise worker-hook router, so it carries
``require_human_api``. An ask reads open while its ``question_id`` carries
no answer fact. No closed-ask history is kept, so ``open=false`` is refused.

post.description:
Clear the runner's own session cookie. Public, like the bounce it complements:
logging out cannot itself require a live session, and clearing an absent cookie is a harmless no-op.
The session is a **stateless** signed cookie, so there is nothing server-side to revoke — deleting
it *is* the logout. It ends this runner's session only, not any hub-side session.

get.description:
The own-identity read. Public and self-resolving: it reports the identity a request
*would* resolve to rather than gating on one, so it never ``401``s. Under a ``none``-mode hub the
surface is authless; under oauth it carries the signed-in username, or ``None`` when none rode
along.

Forward a chunk's detail read to the hub — the whole aggregate, including
transition history, artifacts, and the open escalation.

post.description: Forward a chunk pause to the hub. ``409`` when the chunk is not in a pausable state.

get.description: Deprecated: use `GET /chunks/{chunk_id}/work-items`, which this path aliases onto the identical handler and returns the identical view.

post.description:
Clear a needs_human chunk's local hold.

``409`` while the chunk's takeover is still open (end the interactive session first),
or while the chunk carries no open escalation (nothing needs_human to clear).
Forward a chunk resume to the hub.

Open a takeover over a parked chunk with no running attempt (``409`` otherwise).

``force`` supersedes a live worker attempt instead of refusing, consuming no retry
and recording no escalation.

get.description:
The chunk's segment index, straight off the local ledger — metadata and byte counts
only, never turns. A chunk this runner never held a lease for returns ``[]``.
One segment's turns, local-only — 404 iff absent; 503 iff its owner is unavailable.

503.description: The recorded harness owner is unavailable.

get.description: Forward a chunk's work-items read to the hub — the layered pass-through.

The panel's nine reads composed into one — the eight local sections always
populate; ``fleet_summary`` is ``None`` on a hub outage or an unwired runner.
Every environment in this runner's configured pool, held or free.
Every escalation still open — no later lease mint, and the hub has not ended the chunk.
The newest ``limit`` hub-bound facts recorded by this runner, newest first.
Forward the fleet-summary read to the hub — the layered pass-through.
Every configured harness binding's own computed health.

post.description: Record a lease heartbeat, stamped with the injected clock.

get.description: Active leases, then recently-closed ones, derived at read time.
Forward this lease's chunk's counts-by-agent-type read to the hub over the window.
Forward this lease's chunk's counts-by-file read to the hub over the window.
Forward this lease's chunk's counts-by-node read to the hub over the window.
Forward this lease's chunk's counts-by-skill read to the hub over the window.
Forward this lease's chunk's spend-by-graph read to the hub over the window.
Forward this lease's chunk's spend-by-node read to the hub over the window.

The worker's own artifacts — every node-step input resolved latest-by-epoch, the graph
mint's own baked-in declarations, and blizzard's published system-artifact set, all
kind-discriminated. ``scope`` narrows to one; omitted, all three are read. ``scope=graph``
never reaches the hub; ``scope=system`` always does.

schema.title: Response List Artifacts Api Leases  Lease Id  Artifacts Get

get.description:
One artifact by name, optionally narrowed by ``scope`` and, for node scope, by ``node``;
``404`` when nothing matches. A supplied ``node`` settles scope to node on its own — neither
a graph declaration nor a system artifact has a producing node — so pairing it with
``scope=graph``/``scope=system`` is ``400``. More than one candidate — several upstream
nodes, or a name colliding across scopes — is ``409`` naming them.

Every question asked on the worker's own chunk, oldest-first — open, answered, and
restart-superseded alike. An answer a person gave binds every later session on the chunk.

schema.title: Response Get Chunk Asks Api Leases  Lease Id  Asks Get

post.description:
Record a worker's ask against its lease, minting the question id.

Token-authorized like every other worker verb, since activeness alone would admit an open takeover's
closed reference lease too. ``409`` when the lease is that closed reference lease.

get.description:
The lease's currently staged submissions — newest content per ``name``, not yet
published into any envelope.

get.description: The lease's resolved transcript — 404 iff absent; 503 iff its owner is unavailable.

503.description: The recorded harness owner is unavailable.

get.description:
The runner's machine-local summary: identity, pause states, capacities, hub
connectivity, last tick.

Derived entirely from local store facts plus the injected clock — no hub call, so it
is truthful with the hub unreachable. An unwired service answers 503.

patch.description:
Set this runner's own pause brake — it starts no new workers.

Independent of the hub's brake: it works with the hub unreachable, and neither reads nor
writes the hub's flag. Not a drain: a live worker is left running.

post.description: Mint a selftest run against ``harness`` and begin it off the request thread.

503.description: The requested harness is known but unavailable.

get.description: Read back a selftest run's current state.
Every declared subscription's own newest sampling attempt and credential renewal.
Every takeover still open — the recovery surface for a stranded one.

post.description:
Tell every lease closed in ``[since, until)`` again, inside the request, without moving the live cursor.
A bad window is 422; a replay that must export while tracing is off, or any replay before the runner's first
registration, is 409; and an exporter that refuses is 502 with the counts it accepted before.

get.description:
Tracing on or off, the redacted endpoint, the cursor and its lag, the last export and the last error,
and the bindings' combined harness-telemetry plan with each signal's receiver counts.

delete.description:
Drop the runtime override so the runner's configured prompt resolves again.

Distinct from overriding with empty text, which is itself a standing override; the response
carries whatever the config now resolves to, effective on subsequent spawns.

get.description: The effective spawn preamble prompt: the runtime override if set, else static config.

put.description: Replace the runtime workspace-prompt override — effective on subsequent spawns.
